_why:
Six edges from one statute, all previously carrying no source and no note. Sec. 6802 of the FY2023 NDAA is the provision that establishes AARO and that requires both the Historical Record Report and the annual reports, so it is the origin of five other nodes on this board. Read from the enacted text on govinfo on 22 August 2026 - a 6.5MB document, fetched whole and searched locally rather than sampled.

Three things in the text are worth having on the board and were not. The office is the statutory SUCCESSOR to the UAP Task Force, carrying out its duties 'as in effect on December 26, 2021', rather than a new parallel body. The Director reports to the Deputy Secretary and the PDDNI directly, and to USD(I&S) on administrative matters ONLY, which is a narrower administrative leash than is usually described. And the annual reporting obligation is finite - five reports, 'annually thereafter for four years' - so the series was written with an end date rather than as a standing duty.

Also recorded: sec. 1683(j)(2) obliges the Archivist to make NARA holdings available to the Office 'including classified information', which is a records-access power the board had not captured.

claims.text: Sec. 6802 is titled 'MODIFICATION OF REQUIREMENT FOR OFFICE TO ADDRESS UNIDENTIFIED ANOMALOUS PHENOMENA' and operates by amending section 1683 of the FY2022 NDAA (50 U.S.C. 3373) 'to read as follows', replacing it with 'SEC. 1683. ESTABLISHMENT OF ALL-DOMAIN ANOMALY RESOLUTION OFFICE'.
claims.source: Pub. L. 117-263 sec. 6802, govinfo enacted text, read 22 August 2026, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-117publ263/html/PLAW-117publ263.htm

claims.text: The office is to carry out 'the duties of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, as in effect on December 26, 2021', which makes AARO the statutory successor to the Task Force rather than a parallel body.

The Director of the Office 'shall report directly to the Deputy Secretary of Defense and the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence', and reports to the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security 'on all administrative matters' only.

The Historical Record Report required by new sec. 1683(j)(1)(B)(i) must 'focus on the period beginning on January 1, 1945, and ending on the date on which the Director of the Office completes activities under this subsection'.

The annual reporting obligation at new sec. 1683(k)(1)(A) is joint - 'the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense shall jointly submit' - and finite: the first is due 180 days after enactment of the IAA FY2023, 'and annually thereafter for four years'. Five reports, not a standing requirement.

New sec. 1683(j)(2) obliges the Archivist of the United States to 'make available to the Office such information maintained by the National Archives and Records Administration, including classified information, as the Director of the Office considers necessary'.

edges.label: establishes the office
edges.note: Sec. 6802 does not create AARO alongside anything: it amends section 1683 of the FY2022 NDAA (50 U.S.C. 3373) to read as a new section establishing the office. 'Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, shall establish an office ... to carry out the duties of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, as in effect on December 26, 2021', and 'The office established under paragraph (1) shall be known as the "All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office"'. The reporting chain is set in the same subsection: the Director reports directly to the Deputy Secretary of Defense and the Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence, and to USD(I&S) on administrative matters only. Read from the enacted text on govinfo, 22 August 2026.

edges.label: the report it requires
edges.note: Subsection (j) as enacted by sec. 6802 is where this report comes from. 'Not later than 540 days after the date of the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, the Director of the Office shall submit to the congressional defense committees, the congressional intelligence committees, and congressional leadership a written report detailing the historical record of the United States Government relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena'. The statute fixes its scope: it must 'focus on the period beginning on January 1, 1945, and ending on the date on which the Director of the Office completes activities under this subsection'.

edges.label: the same requirement, unmet
edges.note: Volume II answers to the same subsection (j) obligation. The statute requires a report on the historical record from 1 January 1945 to the completion of the Director's activities; Volume I states on its own concluding page that Volume II 'will be published in accordance with the date es[tablished]'. Volume II is the outstanding half of a statutory requirement, which is why the absence is on the board as a node rather than as a gap.

edges.label: the annual report it requires
edges.note: Subsection (k)(1)(A): 'Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023, and annually thereafter for four years, the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense shall jointly submit to the appropriate congressional committees a report on unidentified anomalous phenomena.' The obligation is JOINT between the DNI and the Secretary, and it is time-limited to five reports rather than standing.

edges.note: The second of the five reports required by subsection (k)(1)(A) as enacted by sec. 6802, which runs 'annually thereafter for four years' from the first report due 180 days after enactment of the IAA FY2023, and is a joint obligation of the DNI and the Secretary of Defense.

edges.label: the annual report it requires
edges.note: The third of the five reports required by subsection (k)(1)(A). Worth reading against the statute: the requirement is for a report submitted jointly by the Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense to the appropriate congressional committees, and it expires after five, so the series has an end date written into it from the start.
